strengths: Identifies a clear and practically significant vulnerability in production safety judges: benign-padding attacks that drive WildGuard's FNR from near-zero to 1.0, a dramatic and well-motivated failure mode.
The proposed WindowScan-Judge (WSJ) is elegantly post-hoc and tuning-free, making it broadly applicable as a wrapper over any existing base judge without retraining.

Quantitative results are striking and concrete — 99.1% absolute FNR reduction while keeping FPR within budget — and results generalize across multiple base judges (WildGuard, Llama Guard 3), lending credibility.

The paper correctly identifies and addresses the multiple-comparisons problem introduced by windowed scanning via Length-Aware FPR Control, showing awareness of the full attack/defense tradeoff space.
weaknesses: The paper is presented only as an abstract/introduction (13 lines of text); no methodology section, experimental setup, datasets, baselines, ablations, or statistical analysis are available for review, making it impossible to evaluate the validity of the claimed results.

The threat model is narrow: only prepend+append padding attacks are evaluated. It is unclear whether WSJ generalizes to more sophisticated adversarial attacks (e.g., interleaved benign/harmful content, semantic obfuscation, or paraphrasing).

The Length-Aware FPR Control mechanism is mentioned but not described — the calibration procedure, how the threshold is set, what the FPR budget parameter is, and whether it holds under distribution shift are all left unspecified.

There is no discussion of computational overhead: windowed multi-scale scanning multiplies inference calls proportionally to the number of windows and scales, which may be prohibitive in real-time content filtering contexts.
No comparison to alternative mitigations is provided (e.g., fine-tuning judges on longer contexts, input truncation, or ensemble approaches), leaving the relative advantage of WSJ unclear.

ai_detection.reasoning: The text follows a highly formulaic NeurIPS-style abstract structure with exactly three bullet-point contributions, each following a rigid template (identify/propose/achieve). The prose is uniformly polished with no hedges, asides, or stylistic variation, and the contribution bullets are suspiciously parallel and self-contained — a pattern strongly associated with LLM-generated academic writing rather than the uneven, iteratively revised style typical of human authors.
